title: Length Beats Complexity (Passphrases)
content: A 4-word passphrase like 'correct-horse-battery-staple' has over 50 bits of entropy and is practically impossible for modern supercomputers to crack, yet easy for humans to remember!

title: Use Spaces in Passphrases
content: Most modern login systems allow spaces. Separating random words with spaces creates high entropy while preventing robotic dictionary attacks.

title: Avoid Cliché Idioms
content: When picking words for a passphrase, pick unrelated random nouns instead of song lyrics, movie quotes, or famous proverbs that attackers have in wordlists.

title: MFA is Your Secondary Shield
content: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) blocks 99.9% of automated credential stuffing attacks, even if an attacker manages to obtain your master password.

title: Prefer Authenticator Apps Over SMS
content: SMS verification codes are vulnerable to SIM-swapping. Use hardware keys (YubiKey) or TOTP authenticator apps (Aegis, Google Authenticator) whenever possible.

title: Guard Your Backup Codes
content: Always download and safely store your one-time recovery codes in a secure, encrypted backup in case you lose access to your primary authenticator device.

title: The Danger of Password Reuse
content: When one low-security website is breached, hackers take your email/password combo and test it automatically against banks, email, and social networks (Credential Stuffing).

title: Unique Passwords for Every Service
content: Treat your digital accounts like different apartments: never use the exact same key to lock all your doors.

title: Never Modulate a Single Root Word
content: Changing 'Summer2023!' to 'Winter2023!' or 'NetflixPass1' is easily guessed by automated rule-based cracking tools like Hashcat.

title: Inspect the URL Domain Carefully
content: Phishing emails create urgent alarms ('Account suspended!'). Always examine the sender address and verify the browser URL domain before typing passwords.

title: Beware of Lookalike Domains (Typosquatting)
content: Attackers register domains like 'paypa1.com' or 'g00gle.com'. Look out for substituted letters, zero instead of O, and unusual top-level domains.

title: Check In-App Rather Than Clicking Links
content: If you receive an alert saying your bank or streaming account is locked, open a fresh browser tab and navigate to the official website directly.

title: Let a Password Manager Remember for You
content: Humans are poor random number generators. Use reputable password managers (Bitwarden, 1Password) to generate and autofill 20+ character random passwords.

title: Strengthen Your Master Vault Password
content: Your master password is the only key you ever have to remember. Make it a 5-to-6 word random passphrase with zero personal identifiers.

title: Enable Biometrics & Auto-Lock
content: Configure your password vault to auto-lock after 5-15 minutes of inactivity to protect your credentials if you step away from your device.

title: Check Your Exposure on Have I Been Pwned
content: Over 13 billion credentials have been exposed in historical data breaches. Periodically check your email addresses on haveibeenpwned.com.

title: Rotate Breached Passwords Immediately
content: If a company announces a security breach, rotate your password immediately and revoke all active sessions and API keys connected to that account.

title: Assume Low-Tier Forums Will Leak
content: Never reuse critical passwords on public forums, gaming servers, or niche hobby boards, which often lack modern Argon2 or bcrypt password hashing.

title: Public Wi-Fi is an Open Broadcast
content: Open Wi-Fi at coffee shops, airports, and hotels can be monitored by attackers using packet sniffers or rogue Evil Twin access points.

title: Always Ensure HTTPS / TLS Encryption
content: Ensure your browser displays the secure lock icon (HTTPS). Avoid entering sensitive credentials if you encounter SSL/TLS certificate warning pages.

title: Use a Trusted VPN or Mobile Hotspot
content: When working from public places, tunnel your traffic through an encrypted VPN or use your cellular mobile hotspot for confidential work.

title: Personal Info is Not a Secret
content: Your pet's name, mother's maiden name, birthday, and high school are easily discoverable on social media. Never use them as passwords or security question answers.

title: Treat Security Questions Like Passwords
content: When websites ask 'What is your favorite food?', don't type 'Pizza'. Type a random string or passphrase stored in your password manager.

title: No Tech Support Will Ever Ask for Your Password
content: Legitimate security administrators, banks, and IT staff will never ask you to disclose your password or your 6-digit MFA token over phone or email.

title: Keep Operating Systems & Browsers Updated
content: Security patches fix zero-day vulnerabilities in memory management and crypto libraries. Enable automatic updates on your OS and web browser.

title: Audit Browser Extensions
content: Malicious or abandoned browser extensions can read keystrokes and session cookies. Uninstall extensions you do not actively need and trust.

title: Keep Firmware on Routers & IoT Fresh
content: Home routers and smart devices are frequent targets for botnets. Update their firmware and disable remote admin management over the WAN.

title: Leetspeak Doesn't Trick Modern Attackers
content: Substituting 'P@ssw0rd1' with '@' for 'a' and '0' for 'o' is tested in the first millisecond of any dictionary attack rule.

title: Avoid Keyboard Walks (qwerty, 1qaz2wsx)
content: Tracing paths across physical keyboard rows or columns ('asdfghjk', 'zaq12wsx') are standard entries in every cracker's wordlist.

title: Repeated Sequences Tank Real Entropy
content: A 16-character password like 'PasswordPassword' sounds long, but has negligible effective entropy because of immediate chunk repetition.

title: NIST SP 800-63B Password Guidelines
content: The official NIST digital identity guidelines recommend long passphrases, checking against breach corpuses, and ending forced periodic 90-day password expiration.

title: OWASP ASVS Standard
content: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard mandates minimum 8-12 character lengths, rate limiting on authentication routes, and secure salted hashing algorithms like Argon2id.
